subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept the exact `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried sandbox config boundary for the official external Windows MXC plugin after the registration-mode fix lands?
rationale: The remaining dependency and argv transport decision is a security and release-support boundary that automation cannot safely approve.

options.title: Accept After Registration Fix
options.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect, then approve the exact current dependency graph and argv config boundary for this opt-in external plugin.

options.title: Require Non-Argv Transport
options.body: Pause merge until upstream MXC or OpenClaw provides a maintainer-approved config transport that does not expose the encoded sandbox envelope through argv.

options.title: Defer Official MXC Plugin
options.body: Keep the work out of the first-party release path until the native dependency, packaging, and sandbox boundary are mature enough for official support.

recommendation.title: Accept After Registration Fix
recommendation.body: Fix the non-full registration side effect, then approve the exact current dependency graph and argv config boundary for this opt-in external plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the live PR and authored the OpenShell sandbox backend used as the closest sibling contract.
